messages:
maya: heads up — after the 1799010000 deploy I see a big dip in prefix cache hit-rate for Hosted compared to Dedicated. numbers: hosted hit 59% -> 38%; dedicated stayed ~91%.
sam: hmm, saw alerts too. any idea if this is netstore related or proxy change? :thinking_face:
eli: ran flamegraphs on the proxy path earlier. serialization changed in the deploy (msgpack -> compact-json). might be key canonicalization differences.
jordan: wait, we intentionally switched to compact-json to reduce payload size for VPC clients — was there an accompanying key-normalization step?
maya: not in that deploy. we only toggled serialization format in the proxy.
kai: that could cause cache key mismatch if the netstore layer hashes the raw blob rather than the canonical key. Hosted uses remote object store + proxy; Dedicated uses local netstore with a prehash step. Private (VPC) sits in front of a tunnel that reorders metadata.
eli: profiling notes: when we request prefix "user:prompt:abc" from Hosted path the proxy sends keys like `"user:prompt:abc"` vs Dedicated sending `user:prompt:abc` (no quotes) after msgpack -> string conversion. hash(seed) differs.
sam: can you paste a minimal example of the observed key bytes?
eli: sure — from tcpdump on proxy -> netstore: ```
0000: 22 75 73 65 72 3a 70 72 6f 6d 70 74 3a 61 62 63 22
         "user:prompt:abc"
```
and Dedicated path shows: ```
0000: 75 73 65 72 3a 70 72 6f 6d 70 74 3a 61 62 63
         user:prompt:abc
```
maya: that difference would explain misses. how did this not show up in staging?
jordan: staging had the same serialization but used a compatibility shim that stripped quotes before hashing. production shard config didn't include the shim because of a feature flag.
kai: so config drift across deployment types. classic.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-cached-keying-regression (priority: P2)
maya: immediate mitigations: 1) rollback proxy serialization change for Hosted, 2) enable shim on Hosted netstore hashing (short-term), 3) write unit test to assert canonical key bytes (long-term).
sam: rollback will cause a deploy window — what's the expected improvement? eli: from traces, reverting serialization should restore hit-rate to ~88-92% within 5 minutes of warm cache.
jordan: warmup strategy suggestion: prefetch top-10k prefixes per tenant for first-hour after deploy, and add a bloom-filter check in proxy to avoid round trips for known-miss keys.
kai: bloom-filter sounds good but needs coordination for Dedicated/Private differences — Dedicated's local store already has near-zero RTT so bloom-filter is less beneficial. For Private VPC with network MTU pathing, the bloom filter reduces egress.
maya: on instrumentation: please add a metric prefix_key_bytes_hex and hashed_key_version to the cache metrics. we need to track when serialization/version drift happens automatically.
eli: adding a small perf test: run a synthetic workload (1k unique prefixes, 10k requests) across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. measure hit-rate, p50/p95 latency, and proxy CPU. will post results.
sam: question about kernel selection comment in root ticket: any relation?
jordan: not directly, but kernel-level io scheduler on Dedicated NVMe vs remote object store changes latency characteristics — rack-local kernel tunables plus our kernel-compiled aio path reduce serialization overhead for Dedicated, so the same miss-rate has much lower cost there.
kai: TL;DR: mismatch in key serialization triggered mass misses on Hosted; Dedicated and Private masked it due to different signing/hashing/transport layers.
maya: action items (owners): 
- maya: coordinate rollback on Hosted proxy (ETA 30m)
- eli: add canonicalization unit tests + tcpdump assertion (ETA today)
- sam: enable shim on Hosted netstore and monitor (ETA 2h)
- jordan: design bloom-filter prefetch prototype (ETA EOD)
- kai: run synthetic perf matrix and post CSV to #eng-runtime (ETA 3h)

eli: quick note on warmup: our current warmup walks prefixes synchronously which thundebursts. propose staggered prefetch with Jittered backoff: ```
for i in top_prefixes:
  sleep(random(0, jitter))
  fetch(i)
```
this reduced median prefetch latency from 180ms -> 45ms in staging.
sam: good. also add an on-deploy small-batch canonicalization pass to avoid rolling back if we need the compact-json for other perf reasons.
maya: after rollback we'll keep compact-json behind a feature flag and add a migration job that rewrites netstore keys atomically (or via versioned-keying).
ops-bot: deploy-bot: queued rollback job #rbk-1799012390 by maya
kai: FYI I captured a perf snippet — Hosted RPC extra serialization CPU ~12% added on proxy when compact-json is used, but Dedicated CPU stayed flat because of offload.
jordan: that explains cost delta. once we patch hashing to be canonical byte-insensitive we'll be able to safely switch serialization.
eli: last thought — add e2e test matrices for serialization x netstore backend x network type (hosted/dedicated/private) so this drift is caught in CI.
maya: agreed. will follow up in the post-incident note. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
